A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SVG2 research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and included appendices are readable and support reliable matching. v1 contains Appendix A; v2 retains it and adds Appendices B–E.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation benchmarks in Table 1, kernel-efficiency measurements, attention analyses, and generated-video comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds FP8, warmup-free, cluster-count, permutation, and numerical-sensitivity results, including its appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions use independent Q/K k-means clustering, semantic-aware permutation, centroid-based top-p selection, centroid caching, and variable-block sparse attention. v2 expands kernel documentation and evaluates FP8 configurations without documenting a redesign of the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both retain Penguin Benchmark/VBench inputs, Wan 2.1 image-to-video and text-to-video tasks, and HunyuanVideo text-to-video generation. The added studies vary precision, warmup, clustering, and execution settings within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SVG, SpargeAttn, and XAttention in their corresponding original comparisons, while adding SVG + FP8 for HunyuanVideo. New kernel plots also include dense FA2/FA3 reference comparisons. The expanded related-work citations do not represent additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds zero-warmup evaluation, FP8 configurations, controlled cluster-count and shared-permutation experiments, and cross-backend sensitivity tests. The original main evaluation still uses 30% dense-attention warmup. Reporting expands to five VBench components and their average, with separate attention-level speedups in the new warmup-free comparison.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's cache, kernel, permutation on/off, and density analyses, v2 tests warmup-free behavior, kernel and end-to-end sensitivity to cluster counts, and independent versus three shared-clustering alternatives. Appendix E additionally examines dense-attention backend sensitivity to explain cross-model quality differences.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. The new average Adjusted Rand Index and backend-sensitivity measurements do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises Hunyuan SpargeAttn/XAttention FLOPs from 470.40/459.58 to 399.16/386.90 PFLOPs. SVG's Wan I2V speedup changes from 1.58× to 1.56×, and SVG2's Wan T2V speedup from 1.58× to 1.60×. Original fidelity scores remain, while FP8 and Appendices B–E add substantial results, including SVG2 + FP8 at 30.389 PSNR and 2.55× speedup. Some original SpargeAttn VBench components disappear. New configurations are not same-setting version gains.

T1.justification: The attention formulation, permutation-equivalence derivation, and centroid-score equations are mathematically unchanged. Changing permutation notation from uppercase to lowercase and adding empirical clustering explanations do not introduce new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free acceleration contribution, identification/computation-waste rationale, Pareto-frontier claim, and headline speedups. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for independent Q/K clustering, hardware-dependent cluster-count tradeoffs, Wan's greater sensitivity to numerical differences, and architecture-dependent end-to-end speedups. These substantially expand interpretation of design choices and cross-model results. The existing limitation concerning extension beyond DiTs remains.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies FA2/A100 and FA3/H100 support, wgmma instructions, per-token address offsets, and shared-memory loading. Appendix D specifies a 74,256-token kernel workload. Default cluster counts and the original H100/CUDA setup were already disclosed; these additions mainly document implementation details.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands beyond sparse attention for DiTs and LLMs to linear attention, state-space models, long-video generation, and caching. References increase from 31 to 61, including works such as LinGen, Self Forcing, and DiCache, with new discussion positioning these approaches as complementary.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. v2 expands related work and the kernel explanation, clarifies wording and captions, and organizes added material into Appendices B–E. The retained core text undergoes limited rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2–6 and Figures 11–12, restructures Table 1 with FP8 rows and aggregate VBench reporting, and replaces Figure 1's examples and prompts. Earlier figures are largely retained or relocated; Appendix A's video panels are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence for cluster-count choices and independent Q/K clustering through Tables 5–6, adds warmup-free testing, and documents the kernel more concretely. These improve support for an already established method. Gains are tempered by incomplete settings for some added experiments, unexplained numerical revisions, and lost SpargeAttn VBench reporting on two tasks.
